Subject: Post-demo: model tradeoff matrix & shortlist for FinLytics POC

Thanks again for the demo time today — productive conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what you emphasized during the call:
- Latency target: p95 <= 450ms for 512-token responses (interactive search suggestions).
- Cost sensitivity: aiming to keep inference unit economics < $0.18 per 1k tokens at scale.
- Quality/risk: hallucination tolerance low for financial extraction tasks; prefer model with strong factual grounding and conservative decoding.
- Throughput: initial volume ~40 qps, spiky up to 120 qps during peak.
- Deployment preference: hosted API first, with option to move to Dedicated pools if predictable load materializes.

Immediate asks from us: 
1) Confirm priority ranking among (latency, cost, hallucination risk).
2) Grant access to a small sample dataset (redacted) you said you could share for a targeted eval run.
3) Confirm available times next week for a 45-minute follow-up to walk the shortlist + bench results.

Attached: finlytics_eval_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt seeds we will use) and latency_cost_matrix.xlsx (early cost/latency estimates).

What we'll deliver before the follow-up: a 3-model shortlist with concrete cost/latency/quality tradeoffs and a small canary eval plan (1k queries from your sample set).

Thanks — Irene

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model tradeoff matrix & shortlist for FinLytics POC

Dan / Monica — looping in the short list and the rationale. I put quick one-line tradeoffs for each model and attached a 2-slide summary (shortlist_reco_slide.pdf). We ran a small synthetic bench on FinLytics' prompt seeds (see Drive link) and these are the headline numbers: 

Model shortlist (recommended order, with rationale):

1) Llama-2-70B (q4f-int8) — best quality for extraction tasks, hallucination rate lowest in our eval (~6% of cases), p95 latency ~520ms on a 8-GPU Dedicated-equivalent setup, estimated cost ~$0.16 per 1k tokens (with prefix KV cache enabled). Tradeoff: slightly above your strict 450ms p95 target but much stronger factuality. Good canary candidate if you prioritize correctness.

2) Mistral-30B-optimized (int8 low-precision path) — excellent latency (p95 ~340ms) and low cost (~$0.11 per 1k tokens). Quality is solid for prompts with constrained templates but shows higher hallucination on free-form extraction (~12%). Tradeoff: great for interactive suggestions where tight latency matters.

3) Falcon-40B-Instruct (gpt-optimized execution) — balanced option: p95 ~410ms, cost ~$0.14 per 1k, moderate hallucination (~9%). Strong if you need a reliable mid-point and simpler rollout.

Notes and assumptions: 
- Cost estimates assume average output length of 240 tokens, active KV/prefix caching on repeated prompts, continuous batching behavior, and regional pricing (US).
- Latency numbers are p95 measured in a controlled bench; real-world p95 will vary with burst patterns and network.
- Hallucination rates are measured against the redacted sample and our internal regression prompts (higher is worse).

Deliverables linked: 
- Benchmarks: https://drive.redwood/company/finlytics/benchmarks/FL-2027-03-benchmarks-v1
- Prompt set: https://docs.redwood/qa/prompt-sets/finlytics_eval_prompt_set_v1
- HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deals/FL-2027-03-28-A

Proposed next steps (owners & timeline):
- Confirm priority: Dan / Monica (reply) — today/tomorrow.
- Approve 1k canary run on hosted API using the redacted sample — FinLytics (sign-off) by Tue 30 Mar.
- We schedule a 45-minute follow-up on Wed 31 Mar to review canary results and pick final model for a 2-week eval.

If you want, we can also include a quantized variant of Llama-2-70B to try for latency improvements — requires a short testing slot.

Attachments: shortlist_reco_slide.pdf
